title.zh: 直角网格双线性诊断采样

summary: Sample a finite real scalar field at caller-selected points inside a rectilinear cylindrical R-Z grid using cellwise bilinear interpolation.

capability: Sample a scalar field at caller-chosen points inside a rectilinear cylindrical R-Z grid.
operation: cellwise bilinear interpolation without a field equation
R-Z grid and field plus [R,Z] query points -> ordered samples
discovery.geometry: Two-dimensional rectilinear cylindrical R-Z grid; grid arrays are indexed [Z,R] and query points are ordered [R,Z].
discovery.boundary: Points on the closed grid boundary are accepted; points outside the grid are rejected rather than clamped or extrapolated.

identity.relation: real scalar field on a rectilinear R-Z grid to point samples
identity.direction: R-Z grids, field and [R,Z] query points -> ordered samples
identity.definition: Within each enclosing cell, blend its four [Z,R]-indexed corner values with the bilinear weights from the point's R and Z fractions. Return one value per point in input order.
identity.model: piecewise bilinear scalar interpolation without a field equation
identity.coordinates: grid arrays indexed [Z,R]; each query point ordered [R,Z]
identity.boundary: Points on the closed grid boundary are accepted; points outside are rejected rather than clamped or extrapolated.
assumptions: The caller supplies the same length unit for the grid coordinates and query points.
quantity is a real scalar sampled at the grid nodes.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.description: Radius coordinate mesh with a common R axis along each row.
inputs.constraints: Finite, rectilinear, strictly increasing radial axis and N_R >= 2; same shape as z_grid and quantity.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.description: Axial coordinate mesh with a common Z axis along each column.
inputs.constraints: Finite, rectilinear, strictly increasing axial axis and N_Z >= 2; same shape as r_grid and quantity.

inputs.name: quantity
inputs.description: Real scalar field sampled at each grid node.
inputs.constraints: Finite and exactly the same shape as the coordinate grids.

inputs.name: points
inputs.constraints: Finite; each point must lie within the closed R-Z grid box. An empty [0,2] array is accepted.

outputs.name: samples
outputs.description: Bilinearly interpolated scalar values in query order; the samples field of the returned scirel._result.Result mapping.
outputs.constraints: One-dimensional array; empty for zero query points. The call returns exactly one Result mapping with the single key samples; mapping access is unchanged and attribute access returns the same array.

preconditions: The real field and query coordinates use the declared [Z,R] grid and [R,Z] point conventions.
The caller has already selected a meaningful quantity and consistent length units.
supported: In-domain point sampling of a real scalar on a strictly ordered rectilinear R-Z grid.
excluded: Interpolation on curvilinear, unstructured, or three-dimensional grids.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for invalid grid rank/shape, nonfinite inputs, insufficient or nonmonotonic axes, nonrectilinear coordinates, invalid point shape, or any point outside the grid.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: The finite in-domain bilinear blend is bounded by its finite corner values. Overflowing coordinate spans, vanishing intermediate weights or terms, and strong cancellation use exact ratios of the original float64 inputs before final rounding.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iteration is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result mapping is returned if any query point fails.

example.description: Sample an affine R-Z scalar field at an interior point and at the upper grid corner, and check the returned mapping type.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel._result import Result
from scirel.numerics.interpolate import sample_rectilinear_field
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid([1.0, 2.0, 4.0], [-1.0, 1.0])
quantity = 3.0*r_grid - 2.0*z_grid + 1.0
result = sample_rectilinear_field(r_grid, z_grid, quantity, [[1.5, 0.0], [4.0, 1.0]])
assert isinstance(result, Result)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['samples'], [5.5, 11.0])
example.expected: The samples are the float64 vector [5.5, 11.0] in query order, inside a Result mapping.

scope: Exact recovery of an affine R-Z field at interior and boundary points.
Rejection of a query point outside the grid.
Direct regression for a bilinear R*Z field and output order.
An empty [0,2] query returns an empty sample vector; an invalid later query rejects the whole call.
Independent affine-center witnesses with overflowing finite coordinate spans, including both axes and signed fields.
Representable values rescued from underflowing coordinate or tensor-product weights, near-node complementary weights, and large cancelling corners.
A constant maximum-float field remains finite at selected interior and grid nodes.

Independent evidence (test_rectilinear_evidence): exact reproduction of a field affine in each axis, agreement with scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator(method='linear') after converting between the [Z, R] grid and [R, Z] point conventions at the call site, nodal exactness at the grid nodes, and rejection of points outside the closed grid with no clamping or extrapolation.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct tests establish selected interpolation identities, arithmetic-scale recovery and boundary behavior. They do not establish correctly rounded evaluation at every binary64 input, any physical validity of the caller-supplied field, or experimental calibration. C1 evidence adds: Affine reproduction plus a SciPy cross-check on a bounded set of points.
known_limitations: Only one real scalar quantity is sampled per call.
No coordinate-unit conversion or extrapolation is performed.
Public distribution licensing and SciRel expert recognition remain pending.

basis.statement: Affine reproduction plus a SciPy cross-check on a bounded set of points decide the sampling.
